text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- A group of minority shareholders in bankrupt ship repairer Lisnave may prevent a general shareholders' meeting from taking place on April 7, in a protest against a lack of information over a restructuring accord between the company and the government. The shareholders' meeting was called to approve the accord.
- Pulp group Portucel Industrial plans to double productivity of an area of 70,000 hectares of eucalyptus trees over the next six years in order to help it meet its demand for raw materials.

- Retail and real estate group Sonae Investimentos has reached an agreement in principle with the government to take over the debts of bankrupt tourism group Torralta, which has hotels in Troia, south of Lisbon, and the southern Algarve region. Sonae and the government are expected to sign the final agreement next week. Sonae is expected to invest more than 25 billion escudos in Torralta.

- The government signed an agreement with the Mello group yesterday to restructure Lisnave. Under the terms of the agreement with Lisnave's majority shareholder, the state will assume part of Lisnave's liabilities from 1994-96 and the ship repairer will try to repay 11 billion escudos of tax and social security arrears to the government under the so-called "Mateus Plan."
- The defence ministry has appointed General Espirito Santo as head of the army.

- The banking group BPI is negotiating with Sonae Investimentos a possible acquisition by BPI of a 25 percent stake in Sonae's in-store bank Banco Universo. This deal may suit both groups as Belmiro de Azevedo, head of Sonae, recently acquired a 4.4 percent stake in BPI.
- A department of the Judicial Police is investigating insurance company O Trabalho over alleged mismanagement.
- The Portuguese population rose by 18.2 percent in 1996 compared with 1995. Population growth was recorded in northern Portugal, Madeira and the Azores. The population fell in other regions.
